title: "dicer doctor"
description: "Check that the host can run instances, and boot a test guest"
---

Checks that the daemon's host can run instances and reach them: KVM,
IPv4 forwarding, the firewall, the tools the daemon runs, its uplink and
its free disk. It then boots a small test guest on each hypervisor the
daemon carries, has it run a command and reach the internet, and deletes
it. Each problem comes with what to do about it.

It exits with an error if a check failed. A warning is something that may
go wrong, such as little free disk, and does not.

The test guest's image is pulled if the host does not have it: on a host
that cannot reach Docker Hub, name another with `--image`.

## Usage

```console
$ dicer doctor [flags]
```

## Examples

```console
$ dicer doctor
$ dicer doctor --host-only
$ dicer doctor --image registry.example.com/busybox:1.37
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--format string` | Output format: table, json or yaml. Default: `table`. |
| `--host-only` | Check the host only, without booting a test guest. |
| `--image string` | Image of the test guest: one with sh and wget, such as busybox. Default: `docker.io/library/busybox:1.37`. |
| `--keep` | Keep a test guest that failed, to look into, rather than delete it. |
| `--timeout duration` | Give up on a test guest that has not run its command after this long. Default: `2m0s`. |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-D`, `--debug` | Trace every call to the daemon on stderr (or set `$DICER_DEBUG`). |
| `-r`, `--remote string` | Daemon to talk to: a remote's name, or an address (unix:///PATH or HOST:PORT) (default `$DICER_REMOTE`, then the current remote, then local). |
| `--request-timeout duration` | Give up on a single call to the daemon after this long, e.g. 30s (0: never; streams such as logs -f and exec are not bounded). |
